speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis results show significant white blood cells, red blood cells, and bacteria. Given your right flank pain and these findings, do you think the pain started suddenly and severely, or did it develop gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the urinalysis showing white blood cells and bacteria, you have a urinary tract infection. Given your history of recurrent UTIs and current right flank pain, have you noticed any visible blood clots in your urine or difficulty urinating? REQUEST TEST: Renal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound - Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound reveals cysts in your medullary collecting ducts, which is highly characteristic of medullary sponge kidney. Given your recurrent UTIs and hematuria, do you experience severe, colicky pain that may radiate to your groin, or is the pain constant? REQUEST TEST: CT_Kidney_NonContrast. REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_CT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Kidney_NonContrast - No nephrolithiasis (kidney stones) detected. The imaging confirms the presence of medullary sponge kidney with characteristic cystic dilations in the collecting ducts, consistent with previous ultrasound findings. No hydronephrosis or obstruction is observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney. The combination of recurrent UTIs, hematuria, right flank pain, and imaging showing cystic dilations in the medullary collecting ducts confirms this congenital anomaly.
